newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan, U.N. council members condemn Jerusalem bombs.
newsitem.headline: Annan, U.N. council members condemn Jerusalem bombs.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan and Security Council members condemned Wednesday's bombing of an outdoor market in West Jerusalem as an act of terrorism and stressed the need to press ahead with the Middle East peace process.
They were reacting to an attack by two Arab suicide bombers on the crowded Mahane Yehuda market that killed 13 people and wounded more than 150.
"I am shocked and horrified by the carnage in Jerusalem today," Annan said in a statement expressing condolences to the government and people of Israel and especially to the families of the victims.
"And I condemn this act of terror unreservedly, as I condemn terrorism from whatever quarter. Violence of this kind can never advance the cause of peace," the U.N. chief said.
Calling this a crucial time in the quest for Middle East peace, Annan appealed "to all concerned to reject violence and pursue their aims through dialogue, at the negotiating table."

Security Council President Peter Osvald of Sweden, in a statement to reporters after council consulations, said members "express their shock and outrage at today's terrible bombing at the Mahane Yehuda market in Jerusalem."
They sent deepest condolences to the families of all those killed and injured in the tragedy and "condemn terrorism and the individual or groups who sponsored and perpetrated this act," Osvald said.

Noting the bombing occurred just after the resumption of negotiations between Israeli and Palestinian officials had been announced, "council members reiterate their support for the Middle East peace process and urge all parties to work for peace," he added.
Earlier, speaking to Cable News Network (CNN), Annan called the bombing "abominable and unfortunate, particularly at a time when all efforts are being made to get the peace talks back on track."
"And I appeal to all involved to avoid the use of bombs and violence and really get back to the negotiating table," he added.

He recalled telling Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in a telephone conversation Monday he was encouraged that he had suspended construction of a controversial housing project in an Arab neighbourhood in East Jerusalem.
"And so I am disappointed that at a crucial time when we were just on the verge of getting the talks back on track that this should happen," Annan told CNN.
American U.N. envoy Bill Richardson told reporters the Jerusalem market bombing was "a dastardly act committed by the enemies of peace who want to block the peace process."

"It is particularly loathsome that whoever perpetrated this deed selected a venue used by completely innocent men, women and children," he said, noting that President Bill Clinton had sent the condolences of the American people.
"The enemies of peace are once again attempting to sabotage the peace process by fomenting fear and hatred. We must not let terrorism triumph," Richardson said.
